title: Harira: Moroccan Lentil and Chickpea Soup with Herbs
summary: A hearty Moroccan soup of lentils, chickpeas, tomato and fine pasta, warmly spiced and packed with fresh coriander and parsley. Finished with lemon, it is a nourishing meal in a bowl.
equipment: large heavy-based pot or casserole with a lid (at least 5 litres)

ingredients.item: tin chickpeas (400 g), drained and rinsed
vermicelli or small pasta, broken into short pieces
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soften the base
steps.text: Heat the oil in the large pot over medium-high heat, then add the onion and celery. Cook, stirring often, for 7-8 minutes until soft and just starting to colour at the edges. This gentle browning builds natural sweetness and a savoury foundation for the whole soup.

steps.title: Bloom the aromatics
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in all the spices for 1 minute, then add half the coriander and parsley for 1 minute more. Frying spices briefly in oil releases their flavour compounds, giving a deeper, rounder taste than adding them to liquid.

steps.title: Simmer the lentils
steps.text: Pour in the broth and water, then add the lentils, chickpeas and 1 tsp of the salt. Bring to a simmer, partly cover and cook gently for 20-25 minutes until the lentils are just tender. A gentle simmer keeps the lentils intact; a hard boil would break them into mush before they cook through.

steps.title: Add tomatoes and pasta
steps.text: Stir in the chopped tomatoes, tomato paste and pasta, then simmer partly covered for 8-10 minutes, stirring now and then so the pasta does not stick, until it is soft. Add the spinach for the last 2 minutes, just until wilted. Adding the acidic tomatoes after the lentils have softened matters, as acid can stop lentils becoming tender.

steps.title: Finish and adjust
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and the remaining herbs. The soup should be thick but still pourable, so add a little hot water if it seems too stiff. Season with the remaining salt and the black pepper and serve with lemon wedges; adding fresh herbs and lemon last keeps their flavour lively.

tips: A common mistake is adding the tomatoes too early, which keeps the lentils firm; wait until they are just tender.
The pasta keeps absorbing liquid as it sits, so expect to loosen leftovers with hot water.
For a gentler heat, reduce the cayenne; for more warmth, serve with extra black pepper at the table.
Rinse the lentils well to remove dust and any small stones.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (the pasta softens a little after freezing). Thaw in the fridge and reheat on the hob, adding hot water to loosen, until piping hot (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
